title: fix: address security review findings from PR #1
body:
## Summary

Addresses all security findings from CodeRabbit and Gemini reviews on PR #1.

### Critical fixes
- **Command injection**: All `execSync` with string interpolation replaced with `execFile`/`gitExec` using argument arrays — no shell invocation for user-supplied values (`repo`, `branch`, `taskId`)
- **Path traversal**: Input validation via `isValidRepo()`, `isValidTaskId()`, `isValidBranch()` regex validators + `path.resolve()` containment checks on all file paths

### High-severity fixes
- **XSS**: Added `escapeHtml()` function; all dynamic values in dashboard HTML are escaped, URLs use `encodeURIComponent()`
- **Auth default**: `checkAuth()` now rejects all requests when no token is configured (secure by default), uses `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for constant-time comparison
- **Auto-generated auth token**: `start.sh` generates a random 256-bit token on first run via `openssl rand -hex 32` and prints it to logs
- **Pinned SSH host key**: GitHub's ed25519 key is hardcoded instead of fetched via `ssh-keyscan` (prevents MITM)

### Other improvements
- **Body size limit**: 1MB cap on request body parsing
- **Model validation**: `model` field validated against safe character pattern before use
- **Dockerfile**: Combined two `npm install -g` commands into one layer (smaller image)
- **README**: Updated Security section documenting all hardening measures, updated auth token docs for secure-by-default behavior

### Files changed
- `server.js` — full security rewrite (input validation, HTML escaping, safe exec, constant-time auth)
- `start.sh` — auto-generate auth token, pin GitHub SSH host key
- `Dockerfile` — combine npm install layers
- `README.md` — security documentation, auth behavior update

Closes #1 review findings.

title: bugfix: fix read-only filesystem crash on Cloudron
body:
## Summary

- Fix crash loop caused by `start.sh` trying to `mkdir` and `chown` inside read-only `/home/cloudron`
- Symlink `/home/cloudron/.ssh`, `.config`, and `.gitconfig` to writable `/app/data/` paths at Docker build time
- Write SSH keys and git config directly to `/app/data/` instead of copying to `/home/cloudron/`

## Root cause

Cloudron mounts `/app/code` (and by extension `/home/cloudron`) as read-only at runtime. The `set -eu` in `start.sh` caused immediate exit on the `chown` failure, so the Node.js server never started and the health check never passed.

## Files changed

- `Dockerfile` — add symlinks from `/home/cloudron/{.ssh,.config,.gitconfig}` to `/app/data/` paths
- `start.sh` — remove copy/mkdir/chown on `/home/cloudron/.ssh`, write directly to `/app/data/.ssh`

title: fix: harden start.sh against symlink attacks in user-writable dirs
body:
## Summary

- Harden all `chown -R` calls with `-h` (no-dereference) flag to prevent symlink-based privilege escalation where a malicious symlink in `/app/data` could redirect ownership changes to sensitive root-owned files
- Add `[[ ! -L ... ]]` symlink guards before every `chmod` and `grep` operation on user-writable paths to prevent permission changes and information disclosure on arbitrary targets
- Fix SSH key ownership regression: `ssh-keygen` runs as root in PHASE 3, leaving generated keys root-owned — added `chown -hR` after generation so the `cloudron` user can actually use them
- Remove rogue symlinks on `known_hosts` before processing to prevent reading sensitive files via `grep` redirect

Addresses all 3 high-severity and 2 medium-severity findings from the Gemini code review on PR #6.

Closes #7

title: fix: improve start.sh clarity by replacing error suppression with explicit checks
body:
## Summary

Addresses quality-debt from PR #5 review feedback (Gemini Code Assist).

- **chmod error suppression**: Replaced `2>/dev/null || true` pattern with explicit `[[ -f ... ]] && chmod` checks. The `-f` test returns false for both missing files and symlinks, so it implicitly provides the symlink guard while being more readable and not hiding unexpected errors.
- **Redundant `touch` before `grep`**: Replaced `touch known_hosts` + unconditional `grep` with a conditional `[[ -f ... ]]` check that only runs `grep` when the file exists, with an empty-file fallback for first-run. Clearer intent, no stderr noise.
- **Simplified `known_hosts` chmod**: After `mv` from `/tmp/known_hosts.tmp`, the file is always a regular file (not a symlink), so the symlink guard on `chmod` was unnecessary.
- **Finding 3 (redundant `.gitconfig` touch/chown)**: Already resolved in the security review PR #5 — no changes needed.

Closes #8

title: fix: restore symlink guards on SSH key chmod and simplify known_hosts logic
body:
## Summary

Addresses high-severity quality-debt from PR #17 review feedback (Gemini Code Assist).

- **HIGH — Symlink attack on SSH key chmod**: Restored explicit `[[ ! -L ]]` guards before `[[ -f ]]` checks on SSH key permission operations. In bash, `[[ -f ]]` follows symlinks — a symlink at `/app/data/.ssh/id_ed25519` pointing to `/etc/shadow` would pass the `-f` test and `chmod` would change permissions on the target file. The `! -L` check prevents this attack vector.
- **MEDIUM — Simplify known_hosts logic**: Replaced the `if/else` block with initialize-first pattern — create the temp file unconditionally, then conditionally populate from existing `known_hosts`. Removes the `else` branch for cleaner control flow.

Both findings from: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops-cloudron-app/pull/17

title: fix: restore symlink guards on SSH key chmod to prevent symlink attacks
body:
## Summary

Fixes high-severity symlink attack vulnerability in `start.sh` introduced by PR #17, based on Gemini Code Assist review feedback.

- **HIGH**: Restore `[[ ! -L ... ]]` symlink guards before `chmod` on SSH key files. PR #17 incorrectly claimed `[[ -f ]]` returns false for symlinks — in bash, `-f` follows symlinks and returns true if the target is a regular file. Without the guard, an attacker could symlink `id_ed25519` to `/etc/shadow` and `chmod 600` would change permissions on the target file (script runs as root).
- **MEDIUM**: Simplify `known_hosts` rebuild logic from if/else to initialize-then-populate pattern (clearer intent, same behaviour).

## Verification

- `shellcheck start.sh` passes clean
- No functional change to happy path — guards only reject symlinks, which should never exist at these paths in normal operation

Closes #20
